summary: Fast Whisper speech-to-text with accurate word-level timestamps and optional speaker labels (who spoke when).

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: WhisperX builds on OpenAI's Whisper to transcribe audio quickly and with precise timing. It uses a faster-whisper backend for batched transcription (the README cites about 70x realtime with large-v2), aligns each word with a wav2vec2 model for accurate word-level timestamps, and can add speaker diarization with pyannote so the transcript shows who said what.
sixtySeconds.problem: Plain Whisper gives timestamps per chunk that are often out of sync and no speaker labels. WhisperX gives word-accurate timing and speaker separation for subtitles and meeting notes.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Pick it when you need word-level timestamps or speaker labels on top of fast Whisper transcription.
requirements: For GPU: NVIDIA GPU with CUDA 12.8
For diarization: a Hugging Face read token and accepting the pyannote model terms

overview: Install from PyPI with pip install whisperx, or run it without installing using uvx whisperx.
Run whisperx on an audio file from the command line; the default model is Whisper small, and --model large-v2 gives higher accuracy.
Add --diarize with your Hugging Face token (--hf_token) to label speakers. It is BSD 2-Clause licensed.
